summary: Unverified password-reset webhook triggers originating from external marketing form integration
description:
Issue summary: Starting 2026-03-13 18:10 UTC we observed an unusual spike in password-reset events that were initiated by an internal webhook endpoint. The requests appear to have been triggered by submissions to an external marketing/vendor form (FormRelay) which forwards leads to our legacy support integration. The webhook calls lacked the expected HMAC signature header in many cases and targeted the internal endpoint responsible for generating password-reset emails.

Impact: Hundreds of password-reset emails were generated for accounts that did not explicitly request resets via the standard UI. No confirmed account takeover activity has been observed to date, but the volume of unsolicited reset emails could enable phishing or account confusion. This affects production only (us-east).

Primary endpoints observed: POST /internal/hooks/form-relay -> /internal/hooks/user-triggered-reset (internal)

Immediate action taken: Rate-limited the legacy webhook endpoint, disabled auto-forwarding from the FormRelay integration, rotated the webhook signing secret, and blocked the vendor IP range in the WAF pending vendor investigation.
impact: Generated ~480 password-reset emails in a 2-hour window (us-east prod). No 5xx server errors; high customer confusion and support volume expected. Potential phishing exposure due to out-of-band resets.
timeline: 2026-03-13 18:05 UTC - First anomalous reset event detected by alerts; 18:10 UTC - spike observed (approx +1200% above baseline); 18:22 UTC - oncall notified via #sec-triage; 18:35 UTC - endpoint rate limit applied; 19:10 UTC - FormRelay integration disabled; 20:00 UTC - webhook secret rotated; 2026-03-14 09:30 UTC - vendor call scheduled; 2026-03-14 14:15 UTC - follow-up investigation in progress.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Submit a lead via the external FormRelay marketing form with a target email address.
2) FormRelay posts to our legacy /internal/hooks/form-relay endpoint.
3) Legacy handler forwards to /internal/hooks/user-triggered-reset without HMAC header under certain payload shapes.
4) Internal system queues a reset email to the user.
Note: Attempt requires reproducing with the specific payload keys used by FormRelay (lead.email, lead.type=marketing, lead.flags.include_reset=true).
logs:
Truncated example logs (prod us-east):
- 2026-03-13T18:11:02Z POST /internal/hooks/form-relay 200 origin=52.23.110.17 userAgent=FormRelay/1.3 signature= -
- 2026-03-13T18:11:03Z POST /internal/hooks/user-triggered-reset 202 user=redacted@example.com requestId=abc123 queue=reset-emails
- 2026-03-13T18:12:45Z POST /internal/hooks/form-relay 200 origin=52.23.110.17 signature=sha256=deadbeef
- 2026-03-13T18:12:46Z POST /internal/hooks/user-triggered-reset 202 user=another@example.com requestId=def456 queue=reset-emails
Note: ~65% of form-relay->user-triggered-reset calls during the window had empty/missing 'X-Webhook-Signature' header.
comments: 2026-03-13 18:28 UTC - @oncall: Detected large uptick in reset emails; clustering to vendor IP 52.23.110.0/24. Applying rate limit and alerting security.
2026-03-13 18:40 UTC - @Rina Patel: Rotated legacy webhook secret and disabled forwarding from FormRelay. Notifying vendor ops for immediate validation.
2026-03-13 19:05 UTC - @Jordan Meyers: Added WAF block for vendor IP range and disabled auto-accept for legacy payloads (feature-flag off). Gathering list of affected user IDs for support outreach.
2026-03-14 09:37 UTC - @VendorContact (FormRelay): Confirmed they sent a retry loop for malformed payloads after a recent schema change; will provide a timeline and fix.
2026-03-14 11:12 UTC - @sec-eng: SIEM rule added to flag any un-signed webhook-to-reset chain. Recommend permanent deprecation of legacy forwarder within 2 weeks.
2026-03-14 13:05 UTC - @customer-support-lead: Drafted customer-facing message and UI banner to clarify unsolicited resets; preparing KB article.
2026-03-14 14:00 UTC - @Jordan Meyers: Next steps: finalize post-incident runbook, validate vendor patch, and schedule rotation of any remaining shared secrets.
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: vendor-side schema change caused FormRelay to strip the signature when certain optional fields were present, creating unsigned requests that the legacy forwarder still accepted.

Evidence: 480+ reset events without X-Webhook-Signature; payloads contain lead.flags.include_reset=true which maps to legacy behavior.
Verified 3 unique requestIds mapping to 3 customer support tickets so far.
Privilege review: No reset tokens were auto-approved for machine logins; reset emails follow standard token generation process and expire per policy. No token reuse detected.
Mitigations tested: rate-limit, secret rotate, vendor IP block, feature-flag disable for legacy forwarding. All mitigations reduced event rate to baseline within ~25 minutes.
Follow-up: schedule deprecation of legacy forwarder, add strict signature enforcement at ingress, add payload schema validation, and require vendor onboarding checklist for future integrations.
resolution_notes: Workaround implemented: disabled legacy forwarder and rotated signing secret; vendor (FormRelay) to deploy fix to retain signature and correct payload shape. Permanent fixes planned: enforce X-Webhook-Signature on all webhook endpoints, add explicit schema validation, and remove legacy auto-forward path. Support will send notification to users who received unsolicited resets with guidance. Postmortem and runbook updates in Confluence.
